# Flag core from ASSS 1.4.4 src/core/flagcore.c (compiled unmodified).
# flagcore owns flag STATE and the packets clients see; the flag GAME that decides
# where flags go is a separate I_FLAGGAME module, and in ASSS 1.4.4 both shipped
# games are Python (src/py/fg_wz.py, fg_turf.py), driven by vectors/pyharness.
# Here the game is a recorder that only logs what flagcore asked of it, so every
# record below is flagcore's own behaviour.
#   # <label>   starts a scenario; 'arena' gives the carry mode, how many flags the
#      game reserved, and the Flag:CarryFlags value flagcore pushed to clientset
#   seat <triples>   freq digit, 'w' ship or 's' spec, '.' normal or 'z' safe zone
#   set <fid> <state> <carrier|-> <x> <y> <freq>   called SetFlags with that record
#   setret <n>       what SetFlags returned (how many records it consumed)
#   touch <player> <fid>   fed flagcore a C2S 0x13 flag-pickup packet
#   kill <killer> <killed> ran flagcore's kill handler
#   reset <freq> <points>  called FlagReset
#   pkt <hex>        each packet sent to the arena, in order and in wire order
#   cb <name>        each callback flagcore fired, in order
#   game <call>      each call flagcore made into the flag game
#   flags <n> <fid>:<state>/<carrier|->/<x>/<y>/<freq>...   every reserved flag
#   carried <player>:<n>...   each player's pkt.flagscarried, which is what the
#      client shows and what the kill packet's flag count is built from
#   counts freq<N>:<n>... <player>:<n>...   CountFreqFlags and CountPlayerFlags
#   chatnet <line>   each line sent to plain-text clients
#   endintervals <n> how many times FlagReset asked persist to end the game interval
#
# Rules these records pin:
#
# 1. set_flag is a 3x3 table on (old state, new state), and each cell sends a
#    DIFFERENT packet. none->onmap and onmap->onmap send a flag LOCATION packet;
#    none->carried and onmap->carried send a flag PICKUP packet; onmap->none sends a
#    location packet with x, y and freq all 0xffff, which ASSS itself calls 'faking'
#    the removal and logs a warning about. There is no real 'remove a flag' packet.
# 2. Taking one flag off a carrier who holds several is the messiest cell. flagcore
#    cannot drop a single flag, so it sends a DROP for the carrier -- which drops
#    all of them on the client -- then re-sends a PICKUP for every OTHER flag that
#    carrier still holds, and logs that it faked it. Watch the packet order.
# 3. flagscarried is maintained by flagcore, not by the game, and the drop path
#    zeroes it and then counts back up. A port that decrements it will drift.
# 4. CARRY_NONE (turf) is a different machine entirely: every flag is always
#    FI_ONMAP, only freq matters, x and y are FORCED to -1 whatever the game asks
#    for, and a request to take a turf flag off the map is refused with an error.
#    How clients are told also changes: during a touch it is a PICKUP packet, during
#    Init nothing at all, and otherwise a turf-ownership packet on a timer.
# 5. A carried flag assigned to the SAME carrier again is a no-op: no packet, no
#    callback, no state change.
# 6. SetFlags always sets a carried flag's freq from the CARRIER's freq, overwriting
#    whatever the game passed in. It refuses FI_CARRIED with no carrier and refuses
#    a non-carried state WITH a carrier, leaving the flag untouched in both cases.
# 7. CountFreqFlags counts both on-map flags owned by the freq and carried flags
#    whose CARRIER is on that freq -- the carried flag's own freq field is not
#    consulted, so the two can disagree and the carrier wins.
# 8. FlagReset on a turf arena only blanks the freqs; on a carry arena it cleans up
#    carriers first and sends a flag-victory packet. Only the carry arena asks
#    persist to end the game interval -- a turf reset does not, so a turf zone's
#    per-game stats interval never ends on a reset.
# 9. A hazard found by running this: in a turf arena, make_turf_packet asserts that
#    EVERY reserved flag is FI_ONMAP. A flag game that reserves more flags than it
#    puts on the map will abort an assert-enabled ASSS the moment a turf ownership
#    packet is built, which FlagReset does directly. fg_turf.py always places all of
#    them, so a stock zone never hits it, but a port is free to be less fragile --
#    and the scenarios below keep every turf flag on the map so the records are of
#    behaviour rather than of an abort.
# CARRY_ALL: every cell of the old-state x new-state table
arena carrymode=1 reserved=4 clientset_override=1
game Init
flags 4 0:none/-/0/0/0 1:none/-/0/0/0 2:none/-/0/0/0 3:none/-/0/0/0
carried
seat 0w.0w.1w.
counts freq0:0 freq1:0 freq2:0 freq3:0 p0:0 p1:0 p2:0
set 0 onmap - 100 200 -1
setret 1
pkt 1200006400c800ffff
cb flagonmap
flags 4 0:onmap/-/100/200/-1 1:none/-/0/0/0 2:none/-/0/0/0 3:none/-/0/0/0
carried 0:0 1:0 2:0
set 0 onmap - 300 400 1
setret 1
pkt 1200002c0190010100
cb flagonmap
flags 4 0:onmap/-/300/400/1 1:none/-/0/0/0 2:none/-/0/0/0 3:none/-/0/0/0
carried 0:0 1:0 2:0
set 0 carried p0 0 0 9
setret 1

# FlagReset on a carry arena

setret 1

cb flagonmap
flags 3 0:carried/p0/0/0/0 1:onmap/-/50/60/1 2:none/-/0/0/0
carried 0:1 1:0

counts freq0:0 freq1:0 freq2:0 freq3:0 p0:0 p1:0
# FlagReset on a turf arena only blanks the freqs
